text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The first round of talks between President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash will last for five days in New York next month.

- Communist Akel party and the socialist Edek party make a last ditch attempt to cooperate in next year's presidential elections, mulling over the name of lawyer Marios Eliades as a potential candidate.
- The United Nations summons leaders to face-to-face talks in New York on July 9.
- Defence Minister Costas Eliades denies the military dialogue designed to ease tension between the two sides is deadlocked.
- Akel, Edek and centre-left United Democrats discuss the possibility of fielding Marios Eliades as the opposition's candidate in the elections.
- The University of Cyprus and the Education Ministry are at loggerheads over the ministry's proposal to merge secondary school final examinations with university entrance examinations.

- The Cyprus Development Bank suggests the creation of a company to administer the port in Larnaca. The government, the Cyprus ports authority, Larnaca municipality and private investors will be shareholders.
- Greek Cypriots are going to the Turkish occupied areas for fun and to gamble at casinos.
